transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sara (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Peregrine Head of Security), Tom (CTO), Priya (DevOps), Noah (Legal)

Summary (auto): Peregrine evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deploy for inference. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and org-level access controls, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS and key custody, data residency and retention policies. Next steps agreed: send SOC2 docs, schedule SE deep dive, provide KMS checklist.

Topics: security posture, KMS integration, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, retention, hosted vs private tradeoffs

Transcript:
[15:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're on for 45 minutes, just a quick intro - I'm Maya, i'm the AE on this account, and with me is Liam our SE and Sara from customer success.
[15:08] Aisha: hi, uh thanks, i'm Aisha, head of security at Peregrine, and i invited Tom who's our CTO, Priya our DevOps lead, and Noah from legal.
[15:15] Tom: hey all.
[15:18] Maya: great, quick agenda - we want to understand your security requirements and hosting constraints so we can recommend hosted, dedicated, or private. feel free to interrupt.
[15:26] Aisha: curious first: do you all have SOC two and ISO stuff? like, are you certified? we need details, not high level.
[15:33] Liam: yeah totally, Redwood's got SOC 2 Type II, and we're in process on ISO 27001 for our control plane, we can share the audit summary. full report is available through our security portal under an NDA.
[15:43] Priya: can we get a redacted copy? we have standard vendor security questionnaire.
[15:46] Maya: absolutely. we'll attach the SOC 2 summary and a redacted report. also we can fill your vendor questionnaire - usually a security package + SOC2 covers most items.
[15:54] Noah: on legal, we'll need evidence of subprocessor list and data flow diagrams.
[15:58] Sara: noted, we'll include the subprocessor list and network diagrams.
[16:04] Aisha: ok on identity, we use SAML SSO with Okta, SCIM for provisioning would be ideal. what's Redwood's support for that?
[16:12] Liam: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support SAML for console/portal access; API auth is token-based and we map tokens to org-level RBAC. occasionally our hosted customers request SCIM and we can enable it via enterprise config.
[16:29] Priya: so SCIM only for enterprise customers, correct?
[16:32] Maya: yes, generally enterprise (Dedicated/Private) or hosted with enterprise contract.
[16:36] Aisha: and RBAC granularity — can we create fine-grained roles, restrict model deployment, see per-user call usage?
[16:43] Liam: yes, RBAC supports per-role permissions - deploy, read logs, billing, admin. token-level attribution is available; for Hosted you get UI controls and audit logs at route/model/token level. Dedicated/Private gives you additional control and on-prem policies.
[16:54] Tom: curious about audit log retention and export — we have a 7 year retention policy for financial data, is that realistic?
[17:02] Sara: seven years is long; our platform keeps operational audit logs for 12 months by default for Hosted, with longer-term export to customer S3 or your archival system possible. Dedicated/Private can be configured to retain or forward logs indefinitely to your storage.
[17:16] Aisha: ok we need immutable logs, tamper evidence, and chain-of-custody for audit.
[17:21] Liam: for Dedicated/Private logs can be forwarded to your SIEM with signing. for Hosted we can stream logs to customer-managed cloud buckets via secure delivery; immutability depends on destination (e.g., AWS S3 Object Lock). we can document recommended patterns.
[17:34] Priya: about encryption and KMS — we currently use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys in a separate account. can Redwood integrate with external KMS or do you force keys?
[17:43] Liam: good question. options: Hosted (default) uses Redwood-managed keys for multi-tenant performance, but we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via an enterprise add-on where keys are in your KMS and we use envelope encryption. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS and keys are never persisted outside your control.
[17:58] Aisha: envelope encryption — can you detail whether plaintext ever touches Redwood infra outside HSM boundary?
[18:04] Liam: plaintext is only in-memory inside the inference runtime; for Private it's within your VPC/air-gapped environment. for Hosted with CMK, the decrypted data is in memory transiently on our nodes; we don't write plaintext to disk. we'll include a diagram of key flow.
[18:18] Tom: does Redwood support HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM / external HSM)?
[18:22] Liam: yes, we support Cloud HSM-backed KMS providers, and Dedicated/Private supports bringing external HSMs.
[18:28] Noah: who has access to keys operationally? do you rotate operator credentials, do you have key custodians?
[18:33] Sara: access to customer-managed keys is governed by the customer's KMS; Redwood personnel do not have access to your CMKs. For Redwood-managed keys we have limited ops processes, audited and included in SOC2. key rotation policy is documented.
[18:45] Aisha: data residency — we need EU-only processing for specific workloads. is regional routing possible?
[18:51] Liam: yes, we support region affinity and can route inference to EU regions only. Dedicated instances can be provisioned in a specific region, and Private gives you full control. Hosted customers can request region pinning for enterprise plans.
[19:02] Priya: performance question — if we route to EU and use CMK in our EU account, will latency increase significantly?
[19:08] Liam: there's a slight increase on first key unwraps, but for token-level inference, KMS calls are infrequent because we use envelope keys and cache unwrapped keys in memory (with TTL). typical p95 latency impact is small but we can run benchmarks with your workload.
[19:22] Tom: ok, benchmarks would be essential. can you run a small perf run with 2k qps equivalent?
[19:27] Liam: we can design a benchmark. for Dedicated we can guarantee throughput SLAs, Hosted we have profiles and can share perf curves. we'll put together a runbook.
[19:36] Aisha: regarding model artifacts and training data — do you store prompted text, are embeddings persisted? we need clarity for e-discovery and data retention.
[19:44] Maya: by default Hosted may cache prefixes for performance, but customers can disable caching. we store request/response logs for billing and troubleshooting per retention policy. Dedicated/Private gives you control to persist nothing or to forward logs. we can offer a more strict no-retention mode for regulated workloads.
[20:00] Priya: do you have PII scrubbing or redact pipelines?
[20:03] Liam: we offer PII detection hooks and can plug in redaction before logs are persisted. typically customers run a light transform before sending to long-term storage. we'll include recommended patterns.
[20:12] Aisha: what's the process for incident response if data leakage or breach happens?
[20:17] Sara: Redwood has an IR runbook; we notify customers per our SLA, provide forensics artifacts, timelines, and remediation steps. we can share an anonymized IR summary example.
[20:29] Noah: required: contractual CLAs for notification timelines, legal hold support for data under litigation, and assistance for forensic collection.
[20:36] Maya: we can map contractual SLAs to required timelines; legal hold is supported via export of retained artefacts.
[20:41] Tom: are there E2E attestations for cryptographic separation between customer tenants?
[20:45] Liam: cryptographic boundaries are enforced at the key management and runtime level; we'll include architecture diagrams and cryptographic primitives in the security pack.
[20:55] Aisha: can we get pen test results or a summary?
[20:57] Maya: yes, we can provide recent penetration test summaries and remediation notes under NDA.
[21:04] Priya: one more ops question — how do you handle operator access for Dedicated clusters? are sessions logged/recorded?
[21:11] Liam: operator sessions are audited and we support session recording and just-in-time access for Dedicated/Private. Hosted is more abstracted but actions are logged.
[21:21] Aisha: compliance automation — do you integrate with our control framework, i.e. evidence collection through API?
[21:27] Sara: we offer an audit API for pulling logs and metadata; some customers wire that to their GRC tooling. we'll include API endpoints in the pack.
[21:37] Tom: cost tradeoffs — if we want 99.9% latencies and EU-only, likely Dedicated? what's the pricing impact ballpark?
[21:46] Maya: Dedicated has a base commitment; it's generally more expensive than Hosted but gives you the SLAs and isolation (typical 2-4x hosted depending on capacity profile). we'll send a pricing ranges doc.
[21:58] Priya: for a POC we want a small dedicated pool in EU for 3 months - acceptable?
[22:04] Maya: yes that's a normal route — pilot on a small Dedicated cluster, then expand. we can do a time-limited pilot.
[22:10] Aisha: any enterprise features we should know about — e.g., policy-as-code for model rollout, auto-fallbacks if a region is down?
[22:18] Liam: we have rollout and routing policies, canary deploys, auto-fallback to a compatible model variant or alternate region. we'll map those features in the docs.
[22:28] Tom: one more: encryption in transit — mTLS?
[22:31] Liam: all traffic is mTLS internally and TLS to customers; private deployments can be configured for mutual TLS end-to-end.
[22:40] Noah: we need to align on a few contractual items: data ownership, indemnity, and breach notification caps — we'll share standard redlines.
[22:48] Maya: happy to take legal redlines. we'll follow up.
[22:52] Aisha: any competitors or vendors you recommend we compare?
[22:56] Maya: commonly Anthropic and some cloud vendor endpoints; also teams sometimes evaluate building their own inference stack. we'll include a comparison matrix.
[23:05] Priya: ok next steps?
[23:09] Maya: recap: we'll send SOC2 Type II summary, security pack (pen test, architecture diagrams, subprocessor list), KMS integration checklist, and pricing + pilot options. Liam will prepare a tech deep dive and benchmark plan; Priya will share Peregrine's KMS details and compliance matrix. Legal will send their questionnaire / redlines.
[23:28] Tom: sounds good. can we pencil in a SE deep dive next Tuesday at 14:00 UTC?
[23:33] Liam: yep that's open for us— i'll block it tentatively.
[23:36] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[23:38] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with notes and attachments.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: some product names transcribed slightly off (SAML as 'SAMEL', KV cache as 'KV cash') - please refer to attached security pack for canonical terms.
